title: The Camera and the Ground: Where on the Floor a Pixel Is, How the Answer Falls Apart Towards the Horizon, and What a Degree of Pitch Does to It

questions.question: Where does the distance to a point on the floor come from in a single image?
options: The size of the object in pixels
The height and tilt of the camera, and the floor being flat
The focus of the lens
Two images taken a moment apart
questions.explanation: A pixel is a ray. Knowing how high the camera is and how far it is tipped, the ray meets a flat floor at one place.

questions.question: The horizon of the camera tipped down 15 degrees with a focal length of 500 pixels was at row:
options: 240, the centre row
0, the top row
questions.explanation: The horizon is above the centre row by the focal length times the tangent of the pitch: 240 less 500 times tan 15 degrees is 106.

questions.question: One row at row 140 spanned how much ground?
questions.explanation: At the centre row a row is 9 mm of floor. At row 140, looking 4.65 m ahead, it is 0.139 m, and at row 120 most of a metre.

questions.question: A pitch a degree wrong put row 140 out in range by:
options: 1 percent
10 percent
Nothing: pitch only shifts the horizon
37 percent
questions.explanation: A ray to 4.65 m is only a few degrees below level, so a degree is a large share of its angle. Close to the camera the same error mattered under 10 percent.

questions.question: Why does a height error of 10 percent give a 10 percent error in range?
options: The ground distance is proportional to the height
The focal length scales with height
The horizon moves with the height
Height errors only matter far away
questions.explanation: The ray's direction does not change with the height. It is followed until it has dropped by the camera's height, so the distance scales with it.

questions.question: Why is the head of a person placed wrongly by the ground plane?
options: A head is smaller than a pixel far away
The lens distorts things near the top of the image
It moves faster than the feet
It is above the floor, so its ray meets the floor further away than the head is
questions.explanation: The method assumes the pixel shows the floor. A point above the floor is seen along a ray that would hit the floor far behind it.
